title: Geo Policy Decision Service for EU-only Customers and Tiered Fallbacks
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Build a centralized Geo Policy Decision Service (GPDS) that evaluates routing constraints for EU-only and data-residency customers and emits deterministic routing decisions used by the Smart Router. GPDS must implement allowlist/denylist checks, customer-level override rules, tier-aware routing (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and deterministic fallback model variant selection in cases of capacity constraints.
acceptance_criteria: GPDS exposes a REST + gRPC evaluation endpoint that returns a routing decision object within 10ms median in the p99 latency budget for 99th percentile requests
Routing decision schema includes: selected_region, selected_tier, model_variant, decision_reason, applied_rules, and trace_id
Allowlist/denylist rules support CIDR ranges, organization IDs, and explicit project IDs and can be evaluated atomically per request
Customer-level policy overrides take precedence over global defaults and are auditable in the policy change log
Smart Router can call GPDS and route requests consistently to honor EU-only constraints for flagged customers and fall back to pre-approved model variants when primary variants are unavailable
End-to-end integration tests validate EU-only customers never route outside EU regions under simulated multi-zone failure
Telemetry emits per-decision metrics and SLOs; dashboards created in Console for policy match rates and fallback frequency
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design API, decision schema, and rule precedence model; review with Legal and Trust
Phase 2: Prototype GPDS (in-memory rule store) and integrate with Smart Router in staging
Phase 3: Persistent policy storage (MDM-backed) and UI surfaces for allowlist/denylist management
Phase 4: Performance optimization (caching decisions, hot-rule paths) and deploy to canary cluster
Phase 5: Observability+auditing and enterprise rollout with migration scripts for customer policies
telemetry_requirements: metric: routing.fallback.rate by customer and model_variant
logs: policy_evaluation.detail for audits (redacted PII) stored in BigQuery for 365 days
trace: include trace_id in Smart Router and downstream runtime logs
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of requests from non-sensitive customers hitting staging Smart Router
Beta: Enroll 3 pilot EU customers and validate zero cross-border routes for their traffic over 2 weeks
Full: Migrate all EU-only flagged customers after 99% success in beta and after completing security review
Fallback mode: If GPDS returns ERROR or times out, Smart Router will use cached last-known decision for up to 30s and then use configured tier fallback policy
Rollback: Automated feature-flag to disable GPDS routing integration and revert to current static policy rules
testing: Unit tests for rule precedence and edge cases (overlaps, CIDR masks, contradictory rules)
Integration tests: Smart Router + GPDS with simulated capacity failures and cross-region latency
Chaos test: deliberate EU-region outage to validate fallback model_variant selection remains EU-compliant when possible
Compliance test: synthetic traffic for EU-only customers validated by audit tooling to ensure data path stays within EU regions
notes: Tradeoffs considered: synchronous decision evaluation vs eventual consistency; we chose synchronous with short cache TTL because legal guarantees require immediate enforcement
Decision: store allowlist/denylist in a single source-of-truth service with changefeed to routers rather than embedding rules in every runtime to reduce drift
Privacy: policy_evaluation.detail logs must be redacted to remove request payloads and only store deterministic rule matches and hashed customer IDs
Fallback variant selection uses a ranked model_variant list per customer: primary -> same-arch quantized variant -> regional-compatible alternative; selection respects customer billing tier
